face.note: a property, not a substance: its face is the scale it is read on

method.instrument: Reversing thermometers on the bottles, then the CTD
method.principle: Originally 20 Nansen/Niskin bottles hung on the wire with reversing thermometers, read on deck after ~45 min; the CTD arrived in the early 1990s under protocols that keep it comparable to the bottle method.

method.instrument: Sea-Bird CTD, pumped dual temperature and conductivity sensors
method.principle: The average of the two temperature sensors in 1 m bins; pumps push water past the sensors whatever the ship’s roll; lowered at 30 m/min to 100 m, then 60 m/min to 515 m.

scale_flags.text: CTD: 18 values above 35 °C on 2 cruises (1994-01-31JD, 2003-04-31JD), inside the declared 40 °C bound

why.text: Temperature sets the water’s density, and so the layering that decides whether deep nutrients reach the sunlit surface; off California the warm years are El Niño years and marine heatwaves.
A warm year off California is usually a lean one: warmer, more layered water brings fewer nutrients up, and the plankton the rest of the food web eats decline.

face.note: dissolved ions, not one molecule: its face is what a kilogram of it holds

method.instrument: Guildline Portasal 8410A salinometer, two per cruise
method.principle: About 225 mL drawn from every Niskin into a numbered KIMAX bottle; the salinometer compares the sample’s conductivity with a reference seawater standard and salinity is computed from the ratio.
In-situ conductivity profiles, corrected against the bottle salts, which also confirm each bottle closed at its target depth.

scale_flags.text: bottle minimum 9.50 is the corrupt 2020-07-33P4 cast whose 99 °C was dropped; its salinity still ships
CTD: 2,797 values below 20 on 8+ cruises, inside the declared bound of 0

why.text: Salinity tags the water masses: the California Current carries fresher Subarctic water south and the Undercurrent carries saltier water from the south; with temperature it sets density.
Salinity and temperature together set seawater’s density, which drives the currents and decides how deep winter mixing reaches.
Salinity is the saltiness or amount of salt dissolved in a body of water, called saline water. It is usually measured in g/L or g/kg.

face.note: one molecule, drawn from ChEBI’s own coordinates

method.instrument: Automated Winkler titrator with a UV end-point detector
method.principle: Carpenter’s (1965) modification of Winkler’s 1889 method: oxygen oxidises manganous hydroxide, acid frees iodine in proportion, thiosulfate titrates it, and the end point is read by the UV absorbance of tri-iodide.
A membrane sensor on the pumped CTD line, soaked at 10 m before the downcast, then station-corrected to the Winkler bottles.

scale.label: air-saturated at 16.1 °C, S 33.5
scale.source: Garcia & Gordon 1992 via TEOS-10 gsw.O2sol, at the record’s surface medians

scale_flags.text: CTD: 37 values above 450 µmol/kg on 5 cruises, inside the declared 700 bound

why.text: Below the mixed layer off Southern California oxygen has fallen since the 1980s and the hypoxic boundary has risen toward the shelf, squeezing the habitat of fish and invertebrates.
Oxygen is the balance of what the ocean takes in at the surface and what animals and bacteria use below; a warmer ocean holds less and mixes less, so it is losing oxygen.
How large are the ocean’s “dead zones” and how fast are they changing?
How is the ocean carbon content changing?
Ocean deoxygenation is the reduction of the oxygen content in different parts of the ocean due to human activities. There are two areas where this occurs.

cites.label: Wikipedia: Ocean deoxygenation, rev. 1354922617, CC BY-SA 4.0

measurements.derivation: Sensor oxygen corrected by regression against the bottle oxygens. Bottle-corrected with ONE regression per cruise, fitted from 4-second-averaged sensor data against all the cruise's bottles (n ~ 1400, fliers omitted).

measurements.label: DO sensor 1 station-corrected
measurements.derivation: Sensor oxygen corrected by regression against the bottle oxygens. Bottle-corrected with a regression fitted PER CAST, from 1 m bin-averaged sensor data against that cast's bottles (n ~ 20, fliers omitted). The providers state station-corrected data are the best. Requires a 500 m cast with roughly ten or more bottles, so a null here is by design on shallow or bottle-poor casts.

chem.name: nitrate
chem.definition: A nitrogen oxoanion formed by loss of a proton from nitric acid. Principal species present at pH 7.3.

method.principle: A cadmium column reduces nitrate to nitrite; sulfanilamide and N-(1-naphthyl)ethylenediamine couple it into a red azo dye read in a 10 mm flow cell. Nitrate is nitrate-plus-nitrite minus the nitrite run without the column.
steps: NO₂⁻ + sulfanilamide + NED → red azo dye
method.wavelength_note: the red dye absorbs green light, 520 nm

scale.label: US drinking-water limit (10 mg/L as N)
scale.source: US EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations, converted

scale_flags.text: no bound declared; the maximum is 95 µmol/L

why.text: Nitrate is the fertiliser upwelling lifts into the light; the spring blooms, and the fisheries above them, run on it. At depth it has risen as oxygen fell, the fingerprint of changing source waters.
Nitrate at the surface is a fingerprint of recent upwelling: where it is high, cold deep water has just arrived and a bloom follows.
How do the eutrophication and pollution impact ocean productivity and water quality?
Is the biomass of the ocean changing?

Upwelling is an oceanographic phenomenon that involves wind-driven motion of dense, cooler, and usually nutrient-rich water from deep water towards the ocean surface. It replaces the warmer and usually nutrient-depleted surface water.

face.note: no NERC concept on the key: it borrows nitrate’s face and says so

chem.name: nitrate
chem.definition: A nitrogen oxoanion formed by loss of a proton from nitric acid. Principal species present at pH 7.3.

method.instrument: ISUS in-situ ultraviolet nitrate sensor on the CTD
method.principle: The ISUS voltage is converted to nitrate by a regression fitted per cast against that cast’s bottle nitrates (about 20, fliers omitted), from 1 m bin-averaged sensor data; a 500 m cast with ten or more bottles is required, so shallow or bottle-poor casts carry none by design.
method.source: principle: the record’s derivation text for est_nitrate_sta_corr

scale.label: US drinking-water limit (10 mg/L as N)
scale.source: US EPA National Primary Drinking Water Regulations, converted

why.text: A sensor on the CTD reads nitrate every metre where the bottles sample a couple of dozen depths, so it resolves the nitracline the bottles straddle.
Nitrate is the fertiliser upwelling lifts into the light; the spring blooms, and the fisheries above them, run on it.

measurements.anomaly_note: Not drawn in the mock: the record carries a climatology for this key, so the page would draw its own bands; the face it borrows is only the picture.

measurements.description: Ammonium concentration (QC'd; the source column is named NH3)

series.description: Ammonium concentration (QC'd; the source column is named NH3)

face.note: two species in equilibrium; the key says ammonia, NERC and the method say ammonium

chem.name: ammonium
chem.definition: An onium cation obtained by protonation of ammonia.

chem.name: ammonia
chem.definition: An azane that consists of a single nitrogen atom covelently bonded to three hydrogen atoms.

method.principle: The Berthelot reaction: hypochlorous acid and phenol react with ammonium in alkaline solution to form indophenol blue, read in a 10 mm flow cell (Koroleff 1969, 1970).
method.wavelength_note: indophenol blue absorbs red light, 660 nm

scale_flags.text: 57.8 % of values are exactly zero; the maximum, 33.58 µmol/L, is off this scale

why.text: Ammonium is nitrogen recycled by zooplankton and bacteria; phytoplankton take it up before nitrate, so production fed by it is “regenerated” rather than “new”.
Most nitrogen in the sunlit layer is recycled several times before it sinks; ammonium measures that recycling, excreted by animals and released as bacteria break organic matter down.
Is the biomass of the ocean changing?
Ammonium is a modified form of ammonia that has an extra hydrogen atom. It is a positively charged (cationic) molecular ion with the chemical formula NH+4 or [NH4]+.

measurements.anomaly_note: Not drawn: 57.8 % of the values are exactly zero (left-censored), so a yearly mean anomaly is a statement about the detection limit, not the ocean.

measurements.label: pH

face.note: minus the log of the hydrogen ion: its face is the scale everyone learned in school

method.instrument: A pH sensor on the CTD (model not on record)
method.principle: The CTD cast files carry a p_h column with its own p_hq quality code, 2009 onward; the FAQ notes newer pH sensors need fewer calibration seawater samples. The scale (total, seawater or NBS) is not stated anywhere in the record.

scale_flags.text: 378 values below 7 and 13 sitting on the declared bound of 9

why.text: Upwelling brings water that is naturally low in pH and carbonate onto the shelf; ocean acidification pushes it further toward water that is corrosive to shells.
Lower pH means less carbonate in the water, and the shells of pteropods off California already show dissolution where corrosive water reaches the surface.
What are rates and impacts of ocean acidification?
Ocean acidification is the ongoing decrease in the pH of the Earth's ocean. Between 1950 and 2020, the average pH of the ocean surface fell from approximately 8.15 to 8.05.

cites.label: Wikipedia: Ocean acidification, rev. 1372947827, CC BY-SA 4.0

measurements.anomaly_note: Not drawn: the release builds no climatology for pH (the record’s climatology flag is false), and the sensor series starts in 2009.

measurements.label: Dissolved inorganic carbon

face.note: three species in one pool: its face is how the pool splits at seawater pH

chem.name: carbon dioxide
chem.definition: A one-carbon compound with formula CO<small><sub>2</sub></small> in which the carbon is attached to each oxygen atom by a double bond. A colourless, odourless gas under normal conditions, it is produced during respiration by all animals, fungi and microorganisms that depend directly or indirectly on living or decaying plants for food.

chem.name: hydrogencarbonate
chem.definition: The carbon oxoanion resulting from the removal of a proton from carbonic acid.

method.instrument: Drawn from the rosette, analysed ashore
method.principle: Samples from the Niskins at selected stations; NCEI accession 0301029 lists a CO₂ gas analyser for DIC and a titrator for alkalinity, calibrated to the reference materials Andrew Dickson’s Scripps laboratory makes for the world.

why.text: The ocean takes up about a quarter of the CO₂ people emit and DIC is where it sits; with alkalinity it fixes pH and the carbonate that shells are built from.
How is the ocean carbon content changing?
What are rates and impacts of ocean acidification?

CalCOFI samples it for first, the long-term characterization of the inorganic carbon system and its response to changing ocean climate, and second, measurements of pH in the coastal zone in order to monitor the impact of ‘corrosive’ waters on benthic ecosystems in the Southern California Bight.

Dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) is the sum of the aqueous species of inorganic carbon in a solution. Carbon compounds can be distinguished as either organic or inorganic, and as dissolved or particulate, depending on their composition.

cites.label: Wikipedia: Dissolved inorganic carbon, rev. 1294570528, CC BY-SA 4.0

measurements.anomaly_note: Not drawn: 1,028 values on 99 cruises since 1983 leave the climatology only 4 cells, all at 10 m.

measurements.label: Est. chlorophyll-a station-corrected
measurements.derivation: Fluorometer voltage converted to chlorophyll-a by regression against bottle chlorophyll-a, applied to the 1 m bin-averaged voltage over 0-200 m ONLY - undefined deeper by construction, not by absence of data. Bottle-corrected with a regression fitted PER CAST, from 1 m bin-averaged sensor data against that cast's bottles (n ~ 20, fliers omitted). The providers state station-corrected data are the best. Requires a 500 m cast with roughly ten or more bottles, so a null here is by design on shallow or bottle-poor casts.

measurements.label: Est. chlorophyll-a cruise-corrected
measurements.derivation: Fluorometer voltage converted to chlorophyll-a by regression against bottle chlorophyll-a, applied to the 1 m bin-averaged voltage over 0-200 m ONLY - undefined deeper by construction, not by absence of data. Bottle-corrected with ONE regression per cruise, fitted from 4-second-averaged sensor data against all the cruise's bottles (n ~ 1400, fliers omitted).

face.note: one molecule, 65 heavy atoms; ChEBI’s layout keeps the magnesium in the ring

method.principle: A known volume is filtered onto a GF/F filter, cold-extracted in 90 % acetone for 24–48 h and read on a fluorometer; the extract is then acidified, which strips the magnesium and turns chlorophyll into phaeopigment, and read again (Yentsch & Menzel 1963; Holm-Hansen et al. 1965; Lorenzen 1967).

scale_flags.text: no bound declared; the maximum is 66.11 µg/L

why.text: Every phytoplankter carries chlorophyll-a, so it is the standard measure of how much plant life the sunlit layer holds: the base of the food web the rest of the survey counts.
Chlorophyll is what satellites see as ocean colour, and bottle chlorophyll like CalCOFI’s is among the ground truth their algorithms were fitted to.

Phytoplankton are the autotrophic (self-feeding) components of the plankton community and a key part of ocean and freshwater ecosystems. The name comes from Ancient Greek φυτόν (phutón), meaning "plant", and πλαγκτός (planktós), meaning "drifter, wanderer, roamer", and thus, "plant drifter".

measurements.label: Wind speed

face.note: no NERC concept on the key and no category in the registry: the face falls back to the scale

a05_only.def: The speed of the air (absolute) in the atmosphere.

method.instrument: Meteorological sensors on the ship’s mast, logged underway
method.principle: About one-minute values while the ship steams between stations. calcofi.org’s underway page renders client-side, so a fetcher reads an empty shell; the sensor model and the unit’s source are not in the record.

scale_flags.text: 217 values at hurricane force (≥ 32.7 m/s) on 7 cruises; read as knots, the median falls from Beaufort 5 to 3 and the 95th percentile from 9 to 6

why.text: Winds blowing toward the equator along the coast push surface water offshore and pull cold, nutrient-rich water up from below: the engine of the California Current’s productivity.
Wind also mixes the surface layer: a windy spell deepens the mixed layer and brings nutrients up even far from the coast.

measurements.anomaly_note: Not drawn: the underway series has no climatology and covers 22 cruises, 2016–2022.

measurements.label: Synechococcus abundance (FCM)

face.note: a count of a living thing: its face is the species face, found through NERC’s WoRMS id

method.principle: A 2 mL subsample from the Niskin is fixed with paraformaldehyde, frozen in liquid nitrogen and kept at −80 °C; ashore the cells are counted one by one as they stream past the laser, Synechococcus resolved by its own pigment fluorescence.

scale.label: in a 5 mL teaspoon, at the median

why.text: One of the most abundant photosynthesisers on Earth, too small for any net: the survey sees it only by counting cells in a bottle of water.
Where the water is warm and poor in nutrients the smallest cells win, so the picoplankton counts show the community shifting in warm years.
Synechococcus is a unicellular cyanobacterium that is very widespread in the marine environment. Its size varies from 0.8 to 1.5 μm.

measurements.anomaly_note: Not drawn: one to three cruises a year since 2004 is too thin for a yearly anomaly of a count.
